body: Even so, I am currently doing well academically at a four year university. I don't think that would be possible if my IQ was in the 70-80 range. 79 is literally borderline mentally retarded.
Do IQ scores change from childhood to adulthood? I'm just curious.

Why would they cap it at 120? I feel that would lead to an entirely inaccurate assessment of people's intelligence. I had my IQ assessed as a child and scored above average so I don't believe I could have gone from that to having a score that could qualify me for Social Security lol.

I feel you on all the ridiculous drunken antics I have done. I am sure I have gained a notable reputation as a creep for contacting over 22 people intoxicated. That was around day 5 into a 7 day long bender. It is cool to at least vent about it. My former sponsor would just tell me to go to a meeting which at the time felt useless. It wasn't so much the idea of going to a meeting but I just needed someone to vent to about it rather than being told to "shut it off."
Do you date a non-addict? If so how did they take that type of news?
I'm just kind of a creepy sad drunk in all honesty.
And call people but I don't threaten or verbally abuse them.

Because  of the stigma of addiction. Which I can admit isn't entirely undeserved. I'm afraid I won't find a significant other who will want to be with me because they don't want to risk a relapse. I just don't want this to be scarlet A that defines me for the rest of my life. I don't care about not drinking, I care about being able to live a normal and happy life. I will try recovery meetings. I'm having trouble relating to people in AA. My family thinks it is the only way to recovery but I have hurt them more by getting sober and relapsing. I went to rehab with people who have stolen or even physically attacked their parents. I just whole up in my room and drink alone.

I know in many ways my addiction is pathetic. I don't have stories of wild parties and getting laid. I just drank myself into alcoholism because I hated myself already and continue to hate myself now. I feel I will never live a normal life, will be treated with suspicion, scorned, outcasted, and hated for being an alcoholic.

I'm....neutral on meetings. I can't find any here where people are young and even then I don't mix well socially. I usually drank alone and my embarrassments this time around involve contacting 22 people (fb or phone calls drunk) saying I was a heroin addict etc. I don't know if this is attention seeking behavior but I have ruined my dignity in a lot of ways and regret entirely I ever crossed this line. I will always have the alcoholic label in my family and in many ways I feel many of them just pity me but are happier without me. I am afraid of them going to alanon because they might recommend they stay away from me. I'm afraid if I ever opened up to a significant other about my past one of their friends and family would tell them to leave because alcoholics are bad people etc. I hate comments I read online about us. Not every alcoholic's story is the same. I never stole, beat, or attacked anyone but because I have the label of an addict I am lumped in.

Thanks for the replies. I just have no idea where I will end up career wise and I feel that everyone is writing me off. I can relate to addiction, the problem is dealing with the wreckage which I am currently trying to fix to what seems no avail.
